subject: Warmup fanout amplification — impact summary, evidence, and next steps
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Sandra Lee <sandra.lee@streamline.ai>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 8 Oct 2027 18:03:00 -0700
Subject: Warmup fanout amplification — initial impact notification

Hi Sandra —

Thanks again for flagging the increased 5xx rate on your dedicated pool earlier today. We identified an atypical warmup pattern on a subset of reserved nodes that caused fanout amplification: many warmup tasks were started in parallel for the same tenant, producing transient request amplification and KV-cache thrash that drove latency and errors for a 22-minute window.

Immediate notes:
- Scope: Streamline AI reserved pool (us-west) — spikes correlated to your service account.
- Impact window: 2027-10-08T17:41:00–2027-10-08T18:03:00 PDT.
- Effect: elevated latency and 5xx responses for a portion of requests (we estimate ~11% of your QPS during the window).

What we're doing now:
1) Collecting allocator warmup traces and tenant telemetry for the slab that served your traffic.
2) Applying a temporary guard to coalesce warmup tasks for the tenant to stop further amplification.
3) Opening an incident JIRA (INC-9842) and pulling an evidence bundle for your review.

We expect a short follow-up with the artifacts and a proposed customer credit within 24 hours. Apologies for the disruption — we know this affects production flows.

If you can share any request IDs or examples of failed calls you have, include them and we’ll prioritize those traces.

Mina Haddad
Senior Manager, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment stubs: allocator-warmup-trace-20271008.jsonl (log), tenant-telemetry-streamline-20271008.csv (csv)

Subject: Re: Warmup fanout amplification — initial impact notification

Thanks Mina —

We saw a spike in error rates on the Search API at ~17:45 PDT and it continued until ~18:00. We have a set of request IDs from our side (attached) and a short postmortem draft we’ll send to our ops channel. Can you confirm whether retries from our side would have amplified the problem? Our service retries on 500s with a short exponential backoff.

Also: what is the ETA for a permanent fix? We can accept a temporary guard but need a timeline for the long-term mitigation.

— Sandra
Head of Platform Engineering
Streamline AI

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 8 Oct 2027 19:05:47 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Warmup fanout amplification — initial impact notification

Quick triage notes — attaching the allocator warmup trace and a summarized timeline. TL;DR: we observed a warmup controller loop that, under a specific race, scheduled N warmup workers for the same tenant across multiple nodes. The controller retry backoff is aggressive on transient allocation failures, and that combined with per-node warmup concurrency produced a transient x-amplification (requests to downstream model runtime increased ~3–4x during warmup).

Evidence included in attachments:
- allocator-warmup-trace-20271008.jsonl (filtered trace) — includes warmup ids and start timestamps.
- tenant-telemetry-streamline-20271008.csv — shows latency and 5xx correlation.

Immediate action completed at ~18:00 PDT: enabled warmup coalescing by tenant and tightened retry window for the allocator controller. That eliminated parallel warmups.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Patch the controller to detect duplicate warmup requests (code-level guard) and add unit + integration tests (ETA: 2 weeks).
2) Add a soft-rate-limit in the warmup path (ETA: 4 days).
3) Postmortem with customer-facing RCA and billing credit proposal (Mina/Karthik to lead).

Ben
Staff SRE, Redwood Inference

--
Attachments: allocator-warmup-trace-20271008.jsonl (log), tenant-telemetry-streamline-20271008.csv (csv)

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Sandra Lee <sandra.lee@streamline.ai>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 9 Oct 2027 10:00:02 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: evidence bundle, proposed credit, and timeline

Hi Sandra —

Appreciate the request IDs you sent — those helped us map the customer-side failures to the warmup amplification window. Attached is a packaged evidence bundle (support-evidence-bundle-20271009.zip) that contains traces and a short timeline. Summary:

- Root cause: a race in the allocator warmup controller that caused duplicate warmup tasks to run concurrently for the same tenant, amplifying downstream request load and transiently overloading the serving path.
- Impact window: 2027-10-08T17:41:00–2027-10-08T18:03:00 PDT.
- Severity: transient production errors and elevated latency; we estimate ~11% of your requests during the window experienced errors or significant latency spikes.

Remediation and timeline:
- Immediate mitigations applied (completed within 20 minutes of detection): warmup coalescing guard + tightened allocator retry backoff.
- Patch to add deterministic duplicate-detection in controller and unit/integration tests: targeted deploy in 2 weeks (2027-10-23).
- Soft-rate-limit on warmup path (short-term protective measure): rollout in 4 days (2027-10-13).

Commercial remediation: we propose a one-time invoice credit for October equal to 10% of the monthly committed reservation fee for the affected pool. If that is acceptable, we’ll send a DocuSign authorization for the credit to streamline the process.

Next steps for Streamline:
- Confirm acceptance of the proposed credit and whether you want us to prioritize the patch in the earlier window.
- If you have additional request IDs or traces, reply and we’ll include them in the final RCA appendix.

We’ll follow up with a formal postmortem document after the patch rollout. Apologies again for the disruption and thank you for the quick coordination.

Mina Haddad
Senior Manager, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: support-evidence-bundle-20271009.zip
Related: JIRA INC-9842
